note: Recast from the species-level treatment of Bourguignon et al. (2016), original in English; the Plazi text is taken from Zenodo record 10529957. The species is a soldierless soil-feeding termite; the original gives only the diagnostic description of the worker and the alate, together with the worker digestive tract and enteric valve characters, and no complete set of body measurements.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head with about 100 long setae. Cushions of the enteric valve with sclerotised appendages, arranged in six clusters of about 20 medium-sized spines each.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Frontal gland pore medium-sized, appearing as a rather pale spot between the compound eyes. Ocelli medium-sized. Posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum slightly concave, corners rounded.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: It differs from P. nigripunctatus in the enteric valve appendages having fewer, stouter spines that do not all point in the same direction. The original places Grigiotermes bequaerti (Snyder & Emerson, 1949) in the synonymy of this species (syn. nov.). Type material: the worker and alate syntypes of Anoplotermes turricola Silvestri, 1901, from Cuyabá, Brazil, housed in the AMNH.
